_doc: Canon ROLE map — the automation that ends stale-role reads. CURATED (a human declares canon), MACHINE-ENFORCED by canon-guard.py. Distinct from resolve-canon.py: that resolves a NAME across the four lanes by md5 (the Warriors rule); THIS resolves a ROLE across DIFFERENT names inside the repo (studio-eyes.py vs studio-eyes-sweep.py; a wired vN vs a newer unwired vN). Canon is what is WIRED, never 'the highest version number'.
how_to_use: canon-guard.py --self-test (gate the guard) ; canon-guard.py --refs (scan repo code/workflows for references to superseded files; HALT) ; canon-guard.py --check <file> (is this file superseded for a role?).

roles.why: v3, browser-rendered (Playwright/Chromium), self-test canary of false-positive traps; README verified 2026-07-26.
roles.status: PROPOSED — founder ratify: floor.yml calls studio-eyes-sweep.py; is the sweep RETIRED, or a fast-CI floor that coexists with the browser gate? If coexisting, split into two roles instead of superseding.

families_awaiting_founder_declaration.note: handoff: v2 is referenced by 11 files though v3/v4 exist. Declare the WIRED one canon, list the rest superseded.
repo is canon over shelf (resolve-canon precedence); the guard should HALT any tool that reads the shelf copy as current.
v5 = three-broadcast canon (ratified 2026-07-26); v6 parked; slices are sources. Declare so a session can't grab a slice as the game.

principles: repo > shelf: if a shelf copy differs from repo, the shelf is stale (resolve-canon.py precedence).
canonical version = the file that is WIRED/referenced, not the highest number.
a role's canon is DECLARED here once and ENFORCED in CI; a reference to a superseded file fails the build, so this manifest cannot silently rot.
